2. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for

3. Mrs. Pushpa Joshi, learned Senior
Advocate assisted by Mrs. Chetna Latwal,
learned counsel for respondent no.2.
SPLA No.93 of 2020
4. State has filed this application seeking
leave to appeal against the judgment dated
07.11.2019 passed by First Additional District
and Sessions Judge, Kashipur, Udham Singh
Nagar in Sessions Trial No.55 of 2016. By the
said judgment, the accused-persons were
acquitted of the charge under Sections 302 &
364-A IPC. However, they were convicted for
the offence punishable under Section 201 IPC
and sentenced to seven years rigorous
imprisonment with fine of Rs.50,000/- each
with default stipulation of one year.
5. Learned State Counsel submits that dead
body of minor child was recovered at the

2
pointing out of accused-persons and CCTV
footages produced by prosecution to show that
deceased-boy was in the company of accused-persons soon before his death were ignored by
learned trial court. He also submits that father
of the deceased has also filed an appeal under
Section 372 read with Section 2 (wa) of
Cr.P.C. which is admitted by the Co-ordinate
Bench of this Court, therefore, leave to appeal
may be granted.
6. We find substance in the submission
made by learned State Counsel. Since the
victim's appeal is admitted by Co-ordinate
Bench of this Court, therefore, the application
seeking leave to appeal deserves to be
allowed. The same is accordingly allowed.
GA No.52 of 2020
7. Admit the appeal.
8. Let paper book be prepared and supplied
to learned counsel for the parties within four
weeks as per rules.
9. List this matter on 09.10.2023.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
